newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An 11-year-old girl on Thursday pointed in court to an influential Philippine congressman as the man alleged to have sexually molested her, court officials said. Romeo Jalosjos, a member of President Fidel Ramos's coalition, sat silent on a court bench after the girl identified him at the start of the trial of one of the country's most sensational court cases. (PHILIPPINE STAR,TODAY)

- President Fidel Ramos denied he had a hand in the preparation of a blue print dubbed "Project Marlboro Rally," to amend the Constitution and lift the term limits on elected officials. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The Cabinet has rejected a proposal from Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa that the Philippines stop exporting sugar to the United States. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- The Philippine Stock Exchange expects to finalise a new distribution scheme for initial public offerings by the middle of next month that will ensure wide dispersal of shares to Filipino investors. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp increased by 40 centavos per litre its price on premium leaded and premium unleaded gasoline. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Caltex Phils Inc is maintaining its pump prices for gasoline and diesel despite price hikes by rivals Petron Corp and Shell Petroleum corp. (BUSINESS DAILY)
